title: C3190 — Front seat control switch RH
introduction:
This reference connects the right-hand front-seat switch’s cavity labels to its electrical assignments. Think of it as the seating chart behind the seat controls: the movement functions, power and ground each have their own place.

I start with the identification table, then use a cavity label in the drawing to find the matching Cavity row under the assignments. Reading across that row connects its position to the circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal information. Read the passenger and movement-direction wording carefully; front-height tilt and rear-height adjustment describe different functions.

The drawing shows the layout on the page, but its physical viewing direction is not specified. Gauge convention and the Size and Used codes are not defined here. This is an identification and reading guide; physical access, probing, wire selection, electrical tests and replacement work need the matching service procedure.

edits.why: I use the projecting housing feature on the drawing’s left and the stepped notch at the bottom as landmarks while reading the page. The shaded cavities correspond to rows without assigned circuits or functions. These visual cues help prevent losing your place; they do not establish which side of a physical connector faces you.

Cavity identifies the position in the drawing; Circuit Number identifies its electrical assignment. The Function wording distinguishes the movement commands from the switch’s power and ground connections. I keep the whole row together, including Terminal Part Number, because neighboring cavities need not share the same terminal identifier. An assignment describes a connection’s role, not proof that it is working.

Kit List in the identification table connects to Number in this table. Service Part identifies the listed service item, while Engineering Shell identifies its housing. The pigtail’s gauge and material entries describe that service item separately from the cavity assignments; they are not instructions for choosing replacement wire or carrying out a splice.
